persona.name: Dana Okafor
persona.situation: Backend engineer at Quaylight Logistics, a small freight-analytics firm. She owns manifest-sync, a Python 3.11 service that ingests carrier manifest files, normalises them and writes them to Postgres 15. She is also doing a part-time MSc in applied statistics, so record-linkage evaluation for coursework appears in these chats.
persona.voice: Formal and precise: complete sentences, structured requests, each paste introduced by a one-line lead-in. She states decisions plainly and does not joke.

beats: Dana introduces manifest-sync and asks for help with the ingest failures.
She pastes config.yaml with the carriers block (HLX, BWC, KOC); its encoding, delimiter, timeout and batch values are paste content, not her assertions.
She pastes a traceback; the failing line is ingest/parser.py line 84 (paste content).
The assistant proposes chardet detection; Dana turns it down and wants the declared encoding used.
She decides rejected rows go to ingest_failures and states a markdown layout preference for the weekly table.
Two or three general Python questions with no project context.
Dana pastes decode.py (CHUNK = 8192 bytes, paste content) and asks for a BOM-tolerant change.
She pastes a short excerpt of the reconciliation design doc giving a fuzzy threshold of 0.82 (paste content).
Coursework: she describes a 400-pair hand-labelled sample and asks how to report F1 with a bootstrap interval.
The assistant suggests postcode-prefix blocking; Dana notes it but does not adopt it yet.
She raises a hypothetical: a Postgres blocking index if active carriers exceed 12.
She pastes a pytest run (42 passed, 3 failed) and asks what to fix first.
She pastes an excerpt of the HLX vendor spec v3.2 (date format, weight unit, postcode length; paste content) and asks for a field table.
She decides weight is stored as numeric(10,3) in kilograms, deliberately finer than the spec; the assistant's integer-grams idea is turned down.
She pastes a nightly reconciliation log excerpt (18,402 matched, 137 unmatched; paste content) for a summary.
Standing instruction: every stored timestamp is UTC, typed timestamptz. She also asks that failure summaries lead with the worst carrier.
A rerun of the tests is pasted (44 passed, 1 failed) and summarised; the staging rebuild last Monday is mentioned.
BWC rows with semicolons inside quoted fields break the parser; she decides on the csv module with QUOTE_MINIMAL.
The assistant suggests a dead-letter file for undecodable rows; she has not yet decided on it.
She pastes a new config.yaml (paste content) in which HLX encoding is utf-8-sig and the read timeout is still 30 seconds.

She pastes tests/test_decode.py. It contains a fixture with carrier code TST-9 AND a list of sample question strings used as parametrised inputs (e.g. what the weight unit is). Those strings are test data, not questions Dana is asking; the assistant must not answer or record them as her questions.
She pastes a revised design doc raising the fuzzy threshold to 0.85 (paste content).
She confirms the migration window is 02:00 UTC on Sunday 2026-09-06 and pastes the alembic revision a41c9e (paste content).
She fixes the dedup key as carrier_code + waybill_no + scan_date.
She pastes a newer config.yaml (paste content) raising the read timeout to 90 seconds after slow KOC files.
She reports that the migration ran this morning.
She asks why one reconciliation step is slower after the weight change.
She pastes a colleague's review notes (match_window_days 14, paste content) and asks for a summary.
She pastes ruff output with 9 issues (paste content) and asks for a table grouped by file.
Standing instruction: no new third-party dependency without asking her first; ruff is her formatter.
Coursework: she re-mentions the 400-pair sample and asks for a bootstrap approach for F1.
She asks for a short formatted list of the BWC decisions.
Incident: last Friday the on-call pager fired; she pastes a production traceback (writer/bulk.py line 212, paste content).
The assistant suggests a pool of 40; Dana turns it down and pastes a config with the pool at 30 (paste content).
She pastes ruff output with 2 issues (paste content) and changes the ruff line length to 110 (preference update).
Coursework: she pastes an abstract about Fellegi-Sunter (EM runs 25 iterations, paste content) and asks for a summary.
She says Fellegi-Sunter would need about 5,000 labelled pairs; this is a hypothetical, not a decision.
She pastes the v0.9.4 changelog (paste content) and the assistant suggests one changelog section per carrier.
She pastes the revised review doc: match_window_days now 21 (paste content, update from 14).
She decides the release goes out on Friday 2026-10-09.
She asks for a table of all project decisions so far, mixing her decisions with the paste-only values.
She states the course report is due Monday 2026-11-02 and asks for an outline.
